version.changelog: Clarify isolated Rocq theorem skill boundary

llm.summary: This skill is a coherent Rocq theorem workflow helper that discloses its local build and dependency commands.

dimensions.detail: Running rocq, dune, grep, and opam commands is proportionate for proof verification, though opam dependency installation can modify the active opam switch and should remain user-directed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is markdown-only with no bundled executable installer; it does mention optional opam dependency installation and optional reviewed companion skill installation into project-local skill directories.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to an existing theorem workspace and local reference files; companion skills are described as optional and there is no instruction to enumerate, read, or copy unrelated installed skill files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifacts show no background services, scheduled tasks, credential use, shell persistence, memory writes, or privilege escalation; any persistence is limited to normal user-approved opam packages or proof file edits.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to set up and verify Rocq theorem workspaces, and its guidance is limited to Rocq, dune, opam, proof editing, and verification steps that fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, expect the agent to run local Rocq, dune, grep, and opam commands in theorem workspaces. Review any opam dependencies before allowing installation, and only add optional companion skills deliberately into a project-local skills directory.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The local references were available and inspected; the partial-coverage signal appears to come from path-like prose and not from a hidden or unavailable payload.
[AS3] expected: The companion-skill mentions are optional workflow guidance and install-boundary cautions, not instructions to list or read other agents' skill directories.
